trigger: ClientHello carrying a status_request extension whose responder_id_list entries consume bytes that the running 'size' counter is never charged for, so the later 'dsize > size' check passes for a request_extensions length that runs past the end of the message.
notes: ssl/t1_lib.c:918-919 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_0c): 'n2s(data, idsize); dsize -= 2 + idsize;' -- dsize is decremented but 'size' is not (the fix adds 'size -= 2 + idsize;'). The over-read then happens at ssl/t1_lib.c:927 d2i_OCSP_RESPID(NULL,&sdata,idsize) and :968-970 d2i_X509_EXTENSIONS(NULL,&sdata,dsize). The parsed pointer is the handshake arena: ssl/s3_srvr.c:819 'd=p=(unsigned char *)s->init_msg;' with s->init_msg = s->init_buf->data + 4, and ssl3_accept pre-grows init_buf with 'BUF_MEM_grow(buf,SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH)' at ssl/s3_srvr.c:246 before the ClientHello is read. For a normal-sized ClientHello the over-read stays entirely inside that live 16384-byte block, so a bounds checker sees a valid in-bounds access -- which is exactly the advisory's 'read the contents of memory following the ClientHello'. Only a ClientHello large enough that the over-read passes offset 16384 escapes the block.

trigger: Multi-threaded application with SSL_MODE_RELEASE_BUFFERS: a read buffer still holding unprocessed data (rbuf.left != 0) is released; another connection on the same SSL_CTX then obtains the very same buffer and the two sessions' data are mixed
notes: THE defining case. Vulnerable line ssl/s3_pkt.c:1057 (1.0.1g) `if (s->mode & SSL_MODE_RELEASE_BUFFERS)` -> fix adds `&& s->s3->rbuf.left == 0`. ssl3_release_read_buffer calls ssl/s3_both.c:848 `freelist_insert(s->ctx, 1, s->s3->rbuf.len, s->s3->rbuf.buf)`, which puts the buffer on the SSL_CTX-wide cache (up to SSL_MAX_BUF_FREELIST_LEN_DEFAULT=32, ssl/ssl.h:958) instead of calling free(); ssl3_setup_read_buffer then hands it straight to another SSL via freelist_extract (ssl/s3_both.c:770). The upstream commit subject is literally 'Fix use after free.' yet free() is never called, so a malloc/free-granularity UAF detector observes nothing at all. Per-branch fixes: 1.0.0 e4e1b8f23039e9fccf5f69f18d1eb698a0474113, 1.0.2 a0fe2e72c48166c9c4bb423397723de1fb6227b0, master 94d1f4b0f3d262edf1cf7023a01d5404945035d5.

trigger: TLS1_HB_REQUEST record whose declared payload length exceeds the actual record length; the response copies `payload` bytes starting 3 bytes into the record
poc: widely published; e.g. Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/ssl/openssl_heartbleed, and the OpenSSL fix commit 96db902 adds the length check
notes: Source pointer is arena memory: ssl/t1_lib.c tls1_process_heartbeat `unsigned char *p = &s->s3->rrec.data[0]` then `pl = p` and `memcpy(bp, pl, payload)`. rrec.data points INSIDE rbuf: ssl/s3_pkt.c:175 `s->packet = rb->buf + rb->offset;` :379 `rr->input= &(s->packet[SSL3_RT_HEADER_LENGTH]);` :400 `rr->data=rr->input;`. rbuf is one block of >=16KB+overhead from ssl/s3_both.c:770 `freelist_extract(s->ctx, 1, len)`, so the first ~16KB of the 64KB over-read is IN BOUNDS of its own allocation. Destination `buffer = OPENSSL_malloc(1+2+payload+padding)` is correctly sized - the write is fine, only the read is out of bounds of the RECORD but inside the BUFFER.

trigger: ClientKeyExchange carrying an RSA ciphertext shorter than SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH (48); the constant-time premaster selection then iterates 48 bytes over the message buffer, reading and writing back past the end of the message
notes: Both a read AND a write past the handshake message, both inside the arena. ssl/s3_srvr.c:2131 `int ssl3_get_client_key_exchange(SSL *s)` and :2164 `p=(unsigned char *)s->init_msg;` - p is inside s->init_buf->data (pre-grown to SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH). Fix adds `if (n < SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH) { al = SSL_AD_DECRYPT_ERROR; ... goto f_err; }` with the comment 'we want to be sure that the buffer size makes it safe to iterate over the entire size of a premaster secret'.

trigger: Malicious server sends a truncated ServerKeyExchange; the PSK/DH/ECDH/SRP parameter parsers read length prefixes and parameter bodies without ever checking the remaining message length n
notes: Non-CVE hardening fix, and a clean arena case. ssl/s3_clnt.c:1316 `param=p=(unsigned char *)s->init_msg;` - init_msg points into s->init_buf->data, a BUF_MEM pre-grown to SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH (ssl/s3_srvr.c:284 `BUF_MEM_grow(buf,SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH)`). The fix adds `param_len = 2; if (param_len > n) goto f_err;` style checks before each n2s. Every over-read stays inside the 16KB handshake block, so it is in bounds of its own allocation.

trigger: Constructing an outgoing ClientHello whose extensions do not fit; individual extension writers advanced the write pointer without consistently re-checking it against limit
notes: A WRITE-side arena overflow, complementing the read-side cases. The ClientHello is composed directly inside the handshake arena: ssl/s3_clnt.c:664 `buf=(unsigned char *)s->init_buf->data;`, :688 `d=p= &(buf[4]);`, :794 `ssl_add_clienthello_tlsext(s, p, buf+SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH)`. The `limit` argument IS the end of the arena block, so any overrun short of that limit is invisible, and the fix reworks the function to track `orig`/`buf` and re-check the limit. Note this is an outgoing-message bug, so it is only reachable with hostile local configuration rather than by a remote peer.

trigger: Truncated ClientHello: client version, the 32-byte random, the session-id length, the DTLS cookie length and the session id itself were all read without checking the declared message length n
notes: Reads IN PLACE from the handshake arena: ssl/s3_srvr.c:930 `d = p = (unsigned char *)s->init_msg;`, and the fix adds three separate bounds tests against `n` / `d + n` (`if (n < 2 + SSL3_RANDOM_SIZE + 1)`, `if (p + SSL3_RANDOM_SIZE + session_length + 1 >= d + n)`, `if (p + j > d + n)`). init_msg lies inside s->init_buf->data, pre-grown to SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH, so every one of these over-reads is in bounds of its own allocation.

trigger: ClientHello declaring a session_id length that runs past the end of the handshake message; the session id was copied and cache-looked-up without checking it against the message end
notes: Fix adds `if (session_id + len > limit) { fatal = 1; goto err; }` at ssl/ssl_sess.c:451. Both pointer and limit are inside the handshake arena: ssl/s3_srvr.c:931 `d = p = (unsigned char *)s->init_msg;` and :996 `i = ssl_get_prev_session(s, p, j, d + n);`. The over-read stays inside s->init_buf.

component: ssl (handshake parsing: ssl3_get_client_hello, session/ticket lookup, TLS extension scanners)
affected_function: ssl3_get_client_hello (ssl/s3_srvr.c), ssl_get_prev_session (ssl/ssl_sess.c), ssl_scan_clienthello_tlsext / ssl_check_for_safari / ssl_scan_serverhello_tlsext / tls1_process_ticket (ssl/t1_lib.c)
trigger: A peer-supplied TLS handshake message whose embedded length field is large enough that the idiom 'p + len > limit' is undefined pointer arithmetic and can wrap, so an over-long session-id / cookie / cipher-list / compression / extension field passes the bounds check and the parser reads past the end of the message body inside s->init_buf.
notes: Every rewritten comparison guards a pointer that lives inside the handshake-message arena, not a malloc block of its own. ssl/s3_srvr.c:938 (OpenSSL_1_0_2h) 'd = p = (unsigned char *)s->init_msg;' and ssl/s3_both.c:430 's->init_msg = s->init_buf->data + 4;'. init_buf is a single BUF_MEM created and grown to the full record size up front at ssl/s3_srvr.c:280 'if (!BUF_MEM_grow(buf, SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH))' (16384 bytes), and ssl/s3_both.c:423 only ever grows it ('BUF_MEM_grow_clean(s->init_buf, (int)l + 4)'), never shrinks it. So the vulnerable check at ssl/s3_srvr.c:1001 'if (p + j > d + n)' bounds the MESSAGE, whose end (d+n) sits far inside a 16 KB allocation; a read past d+n stays inside the same OPENSSL_malloc'd BUF_MEM and is invisible to a malloc/free-granularity checker. tls1_process_ticket and ssl_get_prev_session receive 'limit' derived from the same d+n, so they are the same arena.

trigger: Session with a session_id shorter than 4 bytes; the hash unconditionally reads session_id[0..3]
notes: CAVEATED ROW - blindness here is SUB-OBJECT, not arena. session_id is a fixed array member inside SSL_SESSION, so the read past session_id_length stays inside the struct's own allocation and no bounds checker fires; only an uninitialised-memory tracker would. Note also that ssl/ssl_sess.c SSL_SESSION_new does `memset(ss, 0, sizeof(SSL_SESSION));`, so on a freshly allocated session the bytes read are zero rather than stale - this is a determinism defect more than an information leak, and it is recorded with that limitation stated rather than counted as an arena disclosure.

trigger: ClientHello with a session_ticket extension shorter than 16 bytes of key name plus the IV; the key name and IV were read out of the ticket before any length check
notes: Fix adds `if (eticklen < 16 + EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH) return 2;` at the top of tls_decrypt_ticket in ssl/t1_lib.c. The ticket bytes are extension data inside the ClientHello: ssl/t1_lib.c:3296 `r = tls_decrypt_ticket(s, p, size, session_id, len, ret);` where p walks s->init_msg, i.e. inside s->init_buf. Up to ~32 bytes of over-read remain inside the 16KB handshake block.

trigger: Peer offers a cipher list whose formatted names exceed the caller's buffer; the ':' separator between names is written without a length check, so len goes negative and the 'len-- == 0' guard can never fire again.
notes: EXCLUDED from the arena set: the destination is a caller-supplied buffer, not either OpenSSL arena. Fix is ssl/ssl_lib.c SSL_get_shared_ciphers: 'if (len-- == 0)' -> 'if (len-- <= 0)'. In the in-tree callers the buffer is static/stack, e.g. apps/s_server.c:1486 (tag OpenSSL_0_9_8d) 'MS_STATIC char buf[BUFSIZ];' used at apps/s_server.c:1522 'SSL_get_shared_ciphers(con,buf,sizeof buf)' and apps/s_client.c:1159. alloc_arena is recorded as system-malloc only because that is the closest of the four allowed values for 'the object has its own storage'; the storage class is actually static/automatic, and either way a bounds checker flags the write.

trigger: Any DTLS peer that causes a buffered handshake fragment to be dequeued: the fragment is freed by dtls1_hm_fragment_free and its msg_header.frag_len is then read to build the return value.
notes: Commit 561cbe56 is titled 'Don't access freed data structure.' and is exactly the CVE-2009-1379 fix: it hoists 'unsigned long frag_len = frag->msg_header.frag_len;' above the pqueue_pop/dtls1_hm_fragment_free sequence and changes 'return frag->msg_header.frag_len;' to 'return frag_len;' in dtls1_retrieve_buffered_fragment. The dangling object is the hm_fragment itself, its own allocation: ssl/d1_both.c 'frag = (hm_fragment *)OPENSSL_malloc(sizeof(hm_fragment));' in dtls1_hm_fragment_new (ssl/d1_both.c:179 at tag OpenSSL_1_0_1f, same code in the 1.0.0 betas). Plain heap UAF, fully visible to ASAN/CHERI.

trigger: CMS structure containing OriginatorInfo: the ASN.1 template computed its field offsets against CMS_SignedData instead of CMS_OriginatorInfo, so decoded pointers were written at offsets belonging to a different, larger struct
notes: A template-level type confusion that becomes an out-of-bounds WRITE. crypto/cms/cms_asn1.c ASN1_SEQUENCE(CMS_OriginatorInfo) used `ASN1_IMP_SET_OF_OPT(CMS_SignedData, certificates, ...)` and `(CMS_SignedData, crls, ...)`; the fix changes both to CMS_OriginatorInfo. The offsetof is taken from the wrong struct, so the write lands outside the CMS_OriginatorInfo allocation (which is smaller) - it leaves the block and a bounds checker fires.

component: TLS server extension parsing on resumed sessions (ssl/t1_lib.c)
trigger: Multi-threaded server using OpenSSL's internal session cache: two threads resuming the same shared SSL_SESSION concurrently free and re-allocate session->tlsext_ecpointformatlist / tlsext_ellipticcurvelist / tlsext_hostname, so one thread's memcpy lands in the other thread's shorter buffer.
notes: Overflowed objects are per-session heap buffers with their own allocations: ssl/t1_lib.c (tag OpenSSL_1_0_0a/1_0_0c) 's->session->tlsext_ecpointformatlist = OPENSSL_malloc(ecpointformatlist_length)' immediately followed by 'memcpy(s->session->tlsext_ecpointformatlist, sdata, ecpointformatlist_length)', same shape for tlsext_ellipticcurvelist and 'OPENSSL_malloc(len+1)' for tlsext_hostname. The fix wraps all three in 'if (!s->hit)' so a resumed (shared) session is never mutated. The memcpy SOURCE (sdata) is inside the init_buf arena, but the corrupted DESTINATION is an ordinary malloc'd block, so ASAN/CHERI flag the write normally.

trigger: Certificate chain with policy mappings when X509_V_FLAG_POLICY_CHECK is set: map->subjectDomainPolicy was pushed onto data->expected_policy_set, which takes ownership, and also freed by policy_map_free
notes: Fix removes `if (map->subjectDomainPolicy) ASN1_OBJECT_free(map->subjectDomainPolicy);` from policy_map_free in crypto/x509v3/pcy_map.c and NULLs the field after the push, with the comment 'map->subjectDomainPolicy will be freed when cache->data is freed. Set it to NULL to avoid double-free.' The ASN1_OBJECT is its own allocation, so the second free is a plain heap double-free.

trigger: ASN.1 data read from a BIO whose declared length is negative when converted to int; BUF_MEM_grow accepts the negative length and the caller then writes past the allocated buffer
notes: Fix adds `if (len < 0) return 0;` to BUF_MEM_grow and BUF_MEM_grow_clean in crypto/buffer/buffer.c. The BUF_MEM data is its own allocation - crypto/buffer/buffer.c `ret=OPENSSL_malloc(n)` / `OPENSSL_realloc(str->data,n)` - and the write runs off its end.

component: TLS 1.1/1.2 and DTLS CBC record decryption (ssl/t1_enc.c, ssl/d1_enc.c)
trigger: CBC record whose remaining length is smaller than the explicit IV (block size); 'rec->length -= bs' underflows the unsigned length to ~4e9.
notes: EXCLUDED from the arena set (rule 5: the access leaves the containing block entirely). The record itself IS arena memory -- ssl/s3_pkt.c:379/400 put rr->data inside rbuf.buf, which comes from freelist_extract at ssl/s3_both.c:770. But the defect is an unsigned underflow, not a bounded over-read: ssl/t1_enc.c:892-894 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_1b) 'rec->data += bs; rec->input += bs; rec->length -= bs;' with bs > rec->length. The fix adds 'if (bs > (int)rec->length) return -1;'. Afterwards ssl/s3_pkt.c:437-451 does NOT bail out on the oversized length (the overflow check at :437 only sets a flag inside an #if 0/#else), so :451 computes 'mac = &rr->data[rr->length]' with rr->length ~= 4e9 and :465 MACs over that span. That is ~4 GB past a ~18 KB block: any bounds checker flags it immediately.

trigger: Two DTLS handshake fragments carrying the same message_seq but different msg_len; the second fragment's frag_off/frag_len are validated against its own msg_len while the destination buffer was sized for the first fragment's msg_len.
notes: Overwritten object is frag->fragment, allocated by its own call at ssl/d1_both.c:185 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_1f): 'buf = (unsigned char *)OPENSSL_malloc(frag_len);' inside dtls1_hm_fragment_new(msg_hdr->msg_len, 1) (called at ssl/d1_both.c:622). The overflowing write is ssl/d1_both.c:651-652 'ssl_read_bytes(s, SSL3_RT_HANDSHAKE, frag->fragment + msg_hdr->frag_off, frag_len, 0)'. The size check at ssl/d1_both.c:600 uses the NEW msg_hdr->msg_len, not the size the existing frag was allocated with (the fix adds 'if (frag->msg_header.msg_len != msg_hdr->msg_len) goto err'). Ordinary heap object, not arena memory: ASAN/CHERI flag it normally. Source data comes from the record buffer, but the corrupted object does not.

trigger: SSL_MODE_RELEASE_BUFFERS with a NULL write buffer: do_ssl3_write set up the write buffer before the pending-write check, so a released wbuf was dereferenced as NULL
notes: EXCLUDED from the blind count: this is a NULL dereference, which leaves the block entirely and traps immediately. Recorded only because it is the sibling defect of CVE-2010-5298 on the same freelist mechanism. Fix visible as the relocation of `if (wb->buf == NULL) if (!ssl3_setup_write_buffer(s)) return -1;` in ssl/s3_pkt.c between tags OpenSSL_1_0_1g and OpenSSL_1_0_1h. Exact per-branch commit hash not isolated, so the field is left empty rather than guessed.

trigger: Error path taken after the hm_fragment has already been inserted into s->d1->buffered_messages; the err label frees frag and item while the queue still owns them, and they are freed again when the SSL is destroyed.
notes: Both doubly-freed objects are plain heap objects. frag: 'frag = (hm_fragment *)OPENSSL_malloc(sizeof(hm_fragment));' at ssl/d1_both.c:179 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_1f), freed via dtls1_hm_fragment_free. item: pitem_new (crypto/pqueue/pqueue.c, OPENSSL_malloc). The buggy err label is ssl/d1_both.c:686-690: 'if (frag != NULL) dtls1_hm_fragment_free(frag); if (item != NULL) OPENSSL_free(item);'; the fix changes it to 'if (frag != NULL && item == NULL)'. No arena involvement -- a normal allocator-level double free.

trigger: SRP parameter g, A or B numerically >= N. Buffers are sized from BN_num_bytes(N) but written with BN_bn2bin of the larger value.
notes: crypto/srp/srp_lib.c:92 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_1h): 'if ((tmp = OPENSSL_malloc(longN)) == NULL)' with longN = BN_num_bytes(N) (line 90), then line 101 'longg = BN_bn2bin(g,tmp);' writes BN_num_bytes(g) bytes. Likewise crypto/srp/srp_lib.c:126 'cAB = OPENSSL_malloc(2*longN)' then line 133 'BN_bn2bin(A,cAB+longN)'. The fix adds 'if (BN_ucmp(g, N) >= 0) return NULL;' and 'if (BN_ucmp(A, N) >= 0 || BN_ucmp(B, N) >= 0) return NULL;'. The attacker-controlled BIGNUMs originate in the handshake, but the overflowed buffers are their own OPENSSL_malloc allocations, not arena memory.

trigger: DTLS peer sends application data between ChangeCipherSpec and Finished; the record is buffered into s->d1->buffered_app_data.q as a DTLS1_RECORD_DATA but is torn down as if it were an hm_fragment.
notes: EXCLUDED from the arena set (rule 5: wild pointer). ssl/d1_lib.c:177-183 (tag OpenSSL_1_0_1g) pops buffered_app_data.q and does 'frag = (hm_fragment *)item->data; OPENSSL_free(frag->fragment);' but dtls1_buffer_record stores a DTLS1_RECORD_DATA there ('rdata = OPENSSL_malloc(sizeof(DTLS1_RECORD_DATA));' ssl/d1_pkt.c:216, inserted at :232). The two layouts do not overlap benignly: hm_fragment is {struct hm_header_st msg_header; unsigned char *fragment; ...} (ssl/dtls1.h:175-180) and sizeof(hm_header_st) is 88 bytes on LP64 (ssl/dtls1.h:140-149 plus struct dtls1_retransmit_state at :127-138), while DTLS1_RECORD_DATA (ssl/dtls1.h:264-273) puts rrec.seq_num at exactly offset 88 given SSL3_BUFFER (ssl/ssl3.h:360-367) and SSL3_RECORD (ssl/ssl3.h:348-358). So 'frag->fragment' reads the DTLS record's 8-byte sequence number and frees it as a pointer -- an attacker-controlled wild free, flagged by any allocator or CHERI. The fix reinterprets the item as DTLS1_RECORD_DATA and frees rdata->rbuf.buf instead. Note rdata->rbuf.buf IS the freelist record buffer, and it was being leaked.

trigger: ClientHello supported_elliptic_curves extension with an odd-length curve list; each NamedCurve is 2 bytes, so the final pair read runs one byte past the list
notes: CONTRAST ROW, and the reason the arena test needs its in-place/copied-out qualifier. This extension is NOT read in place: ssl/t1_lib.c:2156 `s->session->tlsext_ellipticcurvelist = OPENSSL_malloc(ellipticcurvelist_length)` then :2163 `memcpy(s->session->tlsext_ellipticcurvelist, sdata, ellipticcurvelist_length);`. The odd byte is copied into an exactly-sized allocation of its own, so the later 2-byte-pair consumer reads one byte past a real malloc'd object and a bounds checker fires. Fix adds `ellipticcurvelist_length & 1` to the reject condition.

trigger: Malformed EC private key file: `*a = ret` was published to the caller before the error path did `EC_KEY_free(ret)`, leaving the caller holding a freed EC_KEY
notes: crypto/ec/ec_asn1.c d2i_ECPrivateKey: fix moves `if (a) *a = ret;` to after success and guards the free with `if (ret && (a == NULL || *a != ret))`. The object is its own allocation from `EC_KEY_new()`, so the dangling pointer is a plain heap UAF a checker flags.

trigger: Certificate whose signature algorithm parameters are an ASN.1 BOOLEAN; ASN1_TYPE_cmp falls through to the ASN1_STRING branch and treats the union's `int boolean` as an ASN1_STRING pointer
notes: crypto/asn1/a_type.c:114 switch on a->type had no V_ASN1_BOOLEAN case. The ASN1_TYPE is its own allocation: crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:342 `typ = OPENSSL_malloc(sizeof(ASN1_TYPE));`. Confusion produces a wild pointer that LEAVES the block entirely, so a bounds/tag checker flags it.

trigger: Re-using an ASN.1 structure across two d2i calls; CHOICE/ADB fields were neither freed nor zeroed, leaving stale field pointers that are later used and freed
notes: Fix adds `ASN1_template_free(pchptr, tt)` + `asn1_set_choice_selector(pval,-1,it)` in crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c ASN1_ITYPE_CHOICE, and an ADB free loop. Each ASN.1 value is individually malloc'd: crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:157,182 `*pval = OPENSSL_malloc(it->size);` - stale pointers are to distinct freed allocations, so a UAF checker sees them.

trigger: AES-NI x86_64 build using the multiblock optimisation with a non-blocking/retrying BIO: a retryable write error frees the jumbo write buffer and sets wb->buf = NULL while wb->left is still non-zero, so the next SSL_write re-enters ssl3_write_pending on the released buffer.
notes: EXCLUDED from the arena set on two counts. (1) The buffer in question is NOT the freelist write buffer: the multiblock path first calls ssl3_release_write_buffer (ssl/s3_pkt.c:698, tag OpenSSL_1_0_2) and then takes its own allocation, ssl/s3_pkt.c:709 'wb->buf = OPENSSL_malloc(packlen);'. (2) The observed access leaves the block entirely: the free at ssl/s3_pkt.c:783-786 also nulls the pointer, so the follow-up at ssl/s3_pkt.c:667 ('if (wb->left != 0) i = ssl3_write_pending(...)') dereferences &wb->buf[wb->offset] with wb->buf == NULL -- a NULL dereference, which is why the advisory reports a segfault rather than corruption. The fix narrows the free to 'if (i < 0 && (!s->wbio || !BIO_should_retry(s->wbio)))'.

trigger: Certificate or CRL with a short/truncated ASN1_TIME; the parser walked past the end of the string because only a lower bound on length was checked
notes: crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c X509_cmp_time read `str = (char *)ctm->data` without tracking remaining length; fix introduces `remaining` and checks it before every read. ctm->data is the ASN1_TIME's own exactly-sized buffer (crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c ASN1_STRING_set `OPENSSL_malloc(len + 1)`), so the over-read leaves the allocation.

trigger: Multi-threaded client resuming a cached session receives a NewSessionTicket; two threads write session->tlsext_tick on the shared SSL_SESSION and both free the old ticket buffer.
notes: The doubly-freed object is the ticket buffer s->session->tlsext_tick, its own allocation (OPENSSL_malloc(ticklen) in ssl3_get_new_session_ticket; the new ssl_session_dup added by the fix mirrors it with 'dest->tlsext_tick = OPENSSL_malloc(src->tlsext_ticklen)' in ssl/ssl_sess.c). The fix stops mutating the shared session at all: before writing the ticket it removes the old SSL_SESSION from the cache and installs a private ssl_session_dup copy. The ticket bytes are read out of the init_buf arena ('p = d = (unsigned char *)s->init_msg;') but the double-freed block is ordinary heap, so ASAN/CHERI flag it.

trigger: Multi-threaded client: the received PSK identity hint is stored in the shared parent SSL_CTX rather than the per-connection SSL_SESSION, so concurrent handshakes free and replace s->ctx->psk_identity_hint under each other.
notes: Vulnerable code in ssl/s3_clnt.c ssl3_get_key_exchange: 'if (s->ctx->psk_identity_hint != NULL) OPENSSL_free(s->ctx->psk_identity_hint); s->ctx->psk_identity_hint = BUF_strdup(tmp_id_hint);' -- a BUF_strdup (OPENSSL_malloc) string on the process-wide SSL_CTX. The fix moves it to per-session state: 's->session->psk_identity_hint = BUF_strndup((char *)p, i);'. Also hardens the server side, ssl/s3_srvr.c ssl3_get_client_key_exchange: 'BUF_strdup((char *)p)' -> 'BUF_strndup((char *)p, i)' -- that one WAS an unbounded strlen walk over the init_buf arena, but it is a hardening change, not the CVE. Double-freed object is plain heap.

trigger: Malformed DSA private key in the 'broken' PKCS#8 encodings: `privkey` aliased `t2->value.integer` inside the ndsa stack, which was then freed, and freed again via privkey
notes: Fix deletes the whole broken-DSA branch in crypto/dsa/dsa_ameth.c dsa_priv_decode that did `privkey = t2->value.integer;` while also owning `ndsa`. The ASN1_INTEGER is its own allocation (crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:157 `*pval = OPENSSL_malloc(it->size);`), so the second free is a plain heap double-free.

trigger: Hex/dec string long enough that the digit count `i` times 4 overflows int, so bn_expand sizes the BIGNUM limb array too small and the conversion writes past it
notes: crypto/bn/bn_print.c BN_hex2bn `if (bn_expand(ret, i * 4) == NULL)`; fix caps `i` at INT_MAX/4 and makes the bn_expand macro return NULL on overflow. The limb array is its own allocation from bn_expand2 -> OPENSSL_malloc, and the overflow runs off its end.

trigger: Very large or unusual format-string input to BIO_printf/BIO_snprintf, where the size computation for the dynamically grown output buffer is wrong
notes: crypto/bio/b_print.c: fix converts fmtstr/fmtint/fmtfp/doapr_outch/_dopr from void to int so allocation failures and size errors propagate. The dynamic buffer is its own allocation grown with OPENSSL_realloc in doapr_outch.

trigger: Very large input to base64 encoding: `ctx->num + inl` overflows int so the partial-block check passes and memcpy writes past ctx->enc_data
notes: crypto/evp/encode.c: `if ((ctx->num + inl) < ctx->length)` -> `if (ctx->length - ctx->num > inl)`. enc_data is a member array of EVP_ENCODE_CTX; with attacker-sized inl the memcpy runs well past the whole context object, so it leaves the allocation and is caught.

trigger: Very large input to EVP_EncryptUpdate: `i + inl` overflows int so the partial-block branch is taken and memcpy writes past ctx->buf
notes: crypto/evp/evp_enc.c EVP_EncryptUpdate: `if (i + inl < bl)` -> `if (bl - i > inl)`. Same integer-overflow shape as CVE-2016-2105 in EVP_EncodeUpdate. ctx->buf is a member array of EVP_CIPHER_CTX; with an attacker-sized inl the memcpy runs past the whole context allocation.

trigger: ASN.1 ANY field holding a negative zero INTEGER; the value is stored with type V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER and later re-encoded through a path that mis-sizes the output
notes: Fix removes V_ASN1_NEG_INTEGER / V_ASN1_NEG_ENUMERATED from the ANY handling in crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c asn1_ex_c2i and crypto/asn1/tasn_enc.c asn1_ex_i2c. Content bytes are the ASN1_STRING's own exactly-sized buffer: crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c ASN1_STRING_set `str->data = OPENSSL_malloc(len + 1);`.

trigger: ASN.1 string longer than the 1024-byte EBCDIC conversion buffer; the length was clamped for the conversion but not for the subsequent read
notes: crypto/x509/x509_obj.c X509_NAME_oneline: `ascii2ebcdic(ebcdic_buf, q, (num > sizeof(ebcdic_buf)) ? sizeof(ebcdic_buf) : num)` clamped only the copy; `num` stayed large and `q = ebcdic_buf` was then read for `num` bytes. Fix assigns the clamp to `num` itself. ebcdic_buf is a stack array; EBCDIC platforms only.

trigger: Large input to MDC2 hashing: `i + len` overflows so the partial-block branch is taken and memcpy writes past c->data
notes: crypto/mdc2/mdc2dgst.c: `if (i + len < MDC2_BLOCK)` -> `if (len < MDC2_BLOCK - i)`. c->data is a member array of MDC2_CTX; the attacker-sized memcpy leaves the context allocation entirely.

trigger: Handshake message larger than ~16k: BUF_MEM_grow_clean reallocates and moves s->init_buf->data, but s->init_msg still points into the old, freed block and is then written through
notes: IMPORTANT CONTRAST ROW - arena memory that is nonetheless CAUGHT. The fix adds grow_init_buf() which saves `msg_offset = (char *)s->init_msg - s->init_buf->data` and restores `s->init_msg = s->init_buf->data + msg_offset` after the grow. Here the arena BLOCK ITSELF is reallocated, so OPENSSL_realloc really does free the old block and an ordinary UAF detector fires. This is the discriminator for the arena test: a dangling pointer to a whole arena block is visible; an over-read WITHIN a live arena block is not. Regression only affected 1.1.0a.

trigger: TLS connection using a *-CHACHA20-POLY1305 ciphersuite where the Poly1305 tag check fails; the failure path zeroes plen bytes starting one plen too far along the output
notes: ADJUDICATED - the two independent passes disagreed on this row, so it was re-read from the diff. crypto/evp/e_chacha20_poly1305.c: `memset(out, 0, plen)` -> `memset(out - plen, 0, plen)`; out had already been advanced by plen, so the buggy memset writes plen bytes PAST the plaintext region. In the TLS path out is in-place inside the ~18.4KB record buffer, so the behaviour is SPLIT: for payloads below roughly 9KB the overwrite stays inside the record buffer and is silent in-arena corruption (blind), while for larger payloads 2*plen exceeds the buffer and it escapes (caught). Recorded as `caught` because the advisory ties the reported impact to 'corrupting larger payloads', i.e. the escaping case is the one that was observed - but the sub-9KB range is precisely the interval in which this bug produced no crash and no detector output.

trigger: X.509 certificate with an IPAddressFamily extension whose addressFamily OCTET STRING is shorter than 2 bytes; the code reads data[1] unconditionally
notes: crypto/x509v3/v3_addr.c: `(f->addressFamily->data[0] << 8) | (f->addressFamily->data[1])` with no length check; fix adds `|| f->addressFamily->length < 2`. addressFamily->data is the ASN1_OCTET_STRING's own exactly-sized buffer (ASN1_STRING_set -> OPENSSL_malloc(len+1)). This is the exact mirror of Heartbleed: a ONE-byte over-read is caught here because the object has its own right-sized allocation.

trigger: A TLS 1.3 peer sends an unrecognised codepoint in signature_algorithms_cert (or signature_algorithms). tls1_lookup_sigalg() returns NULL for a codepoint absent from the static lookup table, and the result is dereferenced unconditionally. Reachable by an unauthenticated client against a server that calls SSL_check_chain() from a client_hello or cert callback.
poc: test/recipes/70-test_sslsigalgs.t (test added by 64eef86733fd40a5b7737dc586754c3fa3414b0c on 1.1.1-stable; master twin 3656c08ab4b1b892730cb5e808b6f4298b08a2e6)
notes: ARENA CAVEAT: this leaves the arena question behind - the dereferenced pointer is NULL returned by a lookup miss, so no allocation is indexed. Dereference site, ssl/t1_lib.c:2133 (OpenSSL_1_1_1f) 'if (sig_nid == sigalg->sigandhash)'; the fix is 'if (sigalg != NULL && sig_nid == sigalg->sigandhash)'. Had the lookup succeeded, sigalg would point into the static const sigalg_lookup_tbl[] (static storage, not heap). The array being iterated, s->s3->tmp.peer_cert_sigalgs, is a plain standalone malloc block from ssl/t1_lib.c:1811 'if ((buf = OPENSSL_malloc(size * sizeof(*buf))) == NULL)' in tls1_save_u16; alloc_arena records that block. Advisory: 'may crash due to a NULL pointer dereference'.

trigger: EVP_CipherUpdate / EVP_EncryptUpdate / EVP_DecryptUpdate called with inl close to INT_MAX. The number of output bytes, ((inl - j) & ~(bl - 1)) + bl, exceeds INT_MAX, so the *outl written back to the caller is negative while the function still returns 1 (success).
notes: CLASS CAVEAT: read against the source, this is an integer overflow of the int output-length counter, not an out-of-bounds access inside OpenSSL. The two guards added by the fix are pure range checks - crypto/evp/evp_enc.c 'if (((inl - j) & ~(bl - 1)) > INT_MAX - bl)' in evp_EncryptDecryptUpdate and 'if ((inl & ~(b - 1)) > INT_MAX - b)' in EVP_DecryptUpdate - and no bounds on a buffer changed. Following the object: 'out' is the caller-supplied output buffer, which the documented contract requires to be at least inl + block_size - 1 bytes, and OpenSSL's own writes stay inside that; in-tree callers allocate it with plain OPENSSL_malloc (e.g. apps/pkeyutl.c:327 'buf_out = app_malloc(buf_outlen, "buffer output");'). Advisory wording is consistent: 'the return value from the function call will be 1 (indicating success), but the output length value will be negative. This could cause applications to behave incorrectly or crash.' The memory-safety consequence is therefore in application code that trusts *outl; verdict caught reflects that such a downstream overflow of a plain malloc block would fire a checker - nothing inside OpenSSL does. 1.1.1j backport: 6a51b9e1d0cf0bf8515f7201b68fb0a3482b3dc1. [bug_class normalised from integer-overflow: the overflow is in the output-length computation and manifests as an overflow of the caller's buffer.]

affected_function: tls12_shared_sigalgs, reached from tls1_set_shared_sigalgs (ssl/t1_lib.c); stale length left behind by init_sig_algs (ssl/statem/extensions.c)
trigger: A TLSv1.2 renegotiation ClientHello that omits signature_algorithms (present in the initial ClientHello) but includes signature_algorithms_cert. init_sig_algs() frees s->s3->tmp.peer_sigalgs and sets it to NULL but leaves peer_sigalgslen at its previous non-zero value, so tls12_shared_sigalgs() walks pref[0..preflen) through a NULL pointer. Server-side only; renegotiation is on by default.
poc: test/recipes/70-test_renegotiation.t (test added by 3ff38629a2df6635f36bfb79513cc6440db8cd70 on 1.1.1-stable; master twin 112580c27b829b0ac0874d5c5787195f27c7952c)
notes: ARENA CAVEAT: this leaves the arena question behind - the buffer/length pair desynchronises but the pointer is explicitly NULLed, so the access is at address 0, not a dangling offset into any pool. Fix site, ssl/statem/extensions.c:1139 (OpenSSL_1_1_1j) 's->s3->tmp.peer_sigalgs = NULL;' with the added 's->s3->tmp.peer_sigalgslen = 0;'. Use site, ssl/t1_lib.c:1779-1780 'pref = s->s3->tmp.peer_sigalgs; preflen = s->s3->tmp.peer_sigalgslen;'. The buffer that was freed is a plain standalone block: ssl/t1_lib.c:1811 'if ((buf = OPENSSL_malloc(size * sizeof(*buf))) == NULL)' in tls1_save_u16 - not the record buffer, not init_buf. Had the pointer been left dangling instead of NULLed this would have been a use-after-free of that malloc block, which is the shape the follow-up commit 39a140597d874e554b736885ac4dea16ac40a87a ('Ensure buffer/length pairs are always in sync') hardens across the rest of libssl.

trigger: Attacker-supplied SM2 ciphertext passed to EVP_PKEY_decrypt() using the documented two-call protocol. sm2_plaintext_size() estimates the plaintext length as ciphertext_len - (10 + 2*field_size + md_size); the real DER overhead can be smaller (C1x/C1y shorter than the field size, or the fixed part larger than 10), so the application allocates a buffer up to 62 bytes too small and the second call writes past it.
notes: The overwritten object is the caller's output buffer, sized from the bad estimate and allocated with plain malloc. Write site, crypto/sm2/sm2_crypt.c:355 (OpenSSL_1_1_1k) 'ptext_buf[i] = C2[i] ^ msg_mask[i];' with msg_len taken from the attacker's DER at :281 'msg_len = sm2_ctext->C2->length;' and no check against *ptext_len; the bad estimate is :85 '*pt_size = msg_len - overhead;'. In-tree allocation site for the two-call protocol: apps/pkeyutl.c:327 'buf_out = app_malloc(buf_outlen, "buffer output");' (app_malloc wraps OPENSSL_malloc), and the internal test does the same at test/sm2_internal_test.c:192 'recovered = OPENSSL_zalloc(ptext_len);'. Advisory: 'The location of the buffer is application dependent but is typically heap allocated.' No arena involved; a malloc-granularity checker fires on the first byte past the block. Companion hardening commit ad1ca777f9702f355a2f74dc5eed713476825f23 adds the missing '*ptext_len < msg_len' check; 1.1.1l backports are 59f5e75f3bced8fc0e130d72a3f582cf7b480b46 and 515ac8b5e544dd713a2b4cabfc54b722d122c218.

component: crypto/x509v3, crypto/x509, crypto/asn1 (ASN.1 string printing and name-constraint processing)
affected_function: i2r_pci (crypto/x509v3/v3_pci.c) plus siblings fixed in the same series: GENERAL_NAME_print, i2v_GENERAL_NAME, POLICYINFO printing, NETSCAPE_SPKI_print, append_ia5, the name-constraints code, and the CMP code
trigger: An application builds an ASN1_STRING whose ->data is not NUL terminated (directly, or via ASN1_STRING_set0()) and then asks OpenSSL to print it or to run name-constraints checking. The printing code passes ->data to a %s conversion, so the read runs past ->length until it finds a NUL, disclosing adjacent heap memory or crashing.
notes: The over-read object is ASN1_STRING->data, a standalone malloc block with no arena around it. Read site, crypto/x509v3/v3_pci.c:80 (OpenSSL_1_1_1k) 'BIO_printf(out, "%*sPolicy Text: %s\n", indent, "", pci->proxyPolicy->policy->data);' fixed to '%.*s' plus ->length. Allocation site, crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c in ASN1_STRING_set(): 'str->data = OPENSSL_realloc(c, len + 1);' - one exact-sized block per string; the vulnerable case is the one where the application supplied the pointer itself through ASN1_STRING_set0(), 'void ASN1_STRING_set0(ASN1_STRING *str, void *data, int len) { OPENSSL_free(str->data); str->data = data; str->length = len; }', i.e. also a plain heap block. Reading past ->length leaves the allocation immediately, so a malloc-granularity checker fires. This CVE was fixed by a contributor ~9 commits, not one; the hash recorded here is the v3_pci.c commit on 1.1.1-stable. Siblings on the same branch: b2b3b9c9936b91315adc0f3254879cb2fd5ca2bd, 1747d4658b3830951068a6a6c1fa2b45c4731fb3, ad6ac17489241574136b7d035f01f6175dd9c941, d2015a783e64613d8e4a142fa05048d1863df944, 95f8c1e142df835d03b5b62521383a462fc5470d, 98624776c4d501c8badd6f772ab7048ac9191cb9, 7c038a6bcd98d4bbfd2c2892a87a1138d2f7c5f3, 030c5aba94788f152f9ceef3549815df45bef702.

trigger: Certificate with a crafted xn-- email address in a name constraint; the decoder writes one code point (4 bytes) past the caller's buffer
poc: test/punycode_test.c (regression tests added with the fix)
notes: Off-by-one bound: crypto/punycode.c `if (written_out > max_out)` -> `>=`. The destination is a STACK array in the caller: crypto/punycode.c ossl_a2ulabel `unsigned int buf[LABEL_BUF_SIZE];  /* It's a hostname */`. Out of scope for the heap-arena question; included as a control.

trigger: Certificate with a crafted xn-- email address; the '.' separator is written without checking the remaining room in the output buffer, giving an unbounded overflow of '.' bytes
poc: test/punycode_test.c (regression tests added with the fix)
notes: crypto/punycode.c ossl_a2ulabel wrote `*outptr = '.'; outptr++;` before re-checking `size >= *outlen - 1`; the fix rewrites the size accounting with `maxsize`. Destination is the caller-supplied `out` buffer, a stack array on the name-constraint path. Control-group row.

trigger: X.509 name-constraint check where a GEN_OTHERNAME SmtpUTF8Mailbox is given an 'effective type' of GEN_EMAIL, so an otherName is then read as an ASN1_IA5STRING
notes: crypto/x509/v3_ncons.c nc_match: fix passes `effective_type` into nc_match_single and adds an OBJ_cmp on otherName->type_id so a non-SmtpUTF8Mailbox otherName is no longer matched as an email. GENERAL_NAME and its members are individually malloc'd (crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:157).

trigger: PEM file with a payload of 0 bytes; the error path frees *header and *data but leaves both pointers published to the caller, which frees them again
poc: test/pemtest.c (regression test added in the same series, commit dc341a46677fe19f055bd2eea0e3a2af21053903)
notes: crypto/pem/pem_lib.c out_free path: fix adds `*header = NULL;` and `*data = NULL;` after the PEM_FREE calls. Both buffers are their own allocations from pem_malloc -> OPENSSL_malloc, so the second free is a plain heap double-free.

trigger: Streaming BIO setup failure (CMS_stream/PKCS7_stream/SMIME_write_ASN1): the ASN.1 BIO was freed on error while still linked into the caller's BIO chain
notes: crypto/asn1/bio_ndef.c BIO_new_NDEF: fix tracks `pop_bio` and pops the BIO out of the chain before freeing, and checks BIO_asn1_set_prefix/suffix return values. The BIO is its own allocation from BIO_new -> OPENSSL_malloc, so the dangling chain pointer is a plain heap UAF.

trigger: d2i_PKCS7(), d2i_PKCS7_bio() or d2i_PKCS7_fp() on a malformed PKCS7 whose contentType is signed / signedAndEnveloped / enveloped but whose [0] EXPLICIT content is absent. p7->d.ptr stays NULL, and the ASN1_OP_D2I_POST callback calls ossl_pkcs7_resolve_libctx(), which reads through the union without checking.
notes: ARENA CAVEAT: this is a NULL dereference, so strictly it leaves the arena question behind - the address read is 0 + offsetof, not an offset inside any allocation. Dereference site, crypto/pkcs7/pk7_lib.c:418 (openssl-3.0.7) 'return p7->d.sign->cert;' with d.sign NULL; the fix adds 'if (p7->d.ptr == NULL) return NULL;'. The containing PKCS7 is a plain zeroed malloc block from the ASN.1 template allocator, crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:114 '*pval = OPENSSL_zalloc(it->size);', which is why d.ptr is NULL rather than garbage. 3.0.8 backport of the fix: 934a04f0e775309cadbef0aa6b9692e1b12a76c6.

trigger: EVP_PKEY_public_check() on a malformed DSA public key whose FFC_PARAMS carries a NULL p. BN_copy() does not check its second argument, so params->p == NULL is dereferenced.
poc: test/ffc_internal_test.c - ffc_public_validate_test / ffc_private_validate_test NULL cases added in the fix commit
notes: ARENA CAVEAT: NULL dereference, so no allocation is actually indexed. Dereference site, crypto/ffc/ffc_key_validate.c:42 (openssl-3.0.7) 'if (BN_copy(tmp, params->p) == NULL'; the fix adds 'if (params == NULL || pub_key == NULL || params->p == NULL) { *ret = FFC_ERROR_PASSED_NULL_PARAM; return 0; }'. The enclosing FFC_PARAMS lives inside a DSA/DH object allocated with plain OPENSSL_zalloc, and any BIGNUM limb array it would have pointed at comes from crypto/bn/bn_lib.c:281 'a = OPENSSL_zalloc(words * sizeof(*a));'. 3.0.8 backport: 23985bac83fd50c8e29431009302b5442f985096.

trigger: CRL with an X.400 address in an X.509 GeneralName; the public header declared x400Address as ASN1_TYPE* while the ASN.1 template decodes it as an ASN1_STRING
notes: Template says ASN1_STRING: crypto/x509/v3_genn.c:37 `ASN1_IMP(GENERAL_NAME, d.x400Address, ASN1_SEQUENCE, GEN_X400)`, but the struct field was `ASN1_TYPE *x400Address`. Fix changes both the field type and the comparison to ASN1_STRING_cmp. The ASN1_STRING is its own allocation; the confusion produces a pointer read out of an int-typed field, which leaves the block.

affected_function: PKCS12_unpack_p7data / PKCS12_unpack_p7encdata / PKCS12_unpack_authsafes / pkcs12_gen_mac / newpass_p12 / SMIME_write_PKCS7 (crypto/pkcs12, crypto/pkcs7)
trigger: A PKCS12 file whose PKCS7 ContentInfo has a valid 'type' but a NULL optional content field (e.g. p7->d.data / p7->d.encrypted / p12->authsafes->d.data / p7->d.sign): the code dereferenced the NULL field.
notes: PLAIN NULL DEREFERENCE - it LEAVES THE BLOCK: the fault is a read through a NULL sub-field (address ~0), not an over-read/over-write inside any allocated object, so an arena/bounds allocator does not apply; the MMU catches it. Fix adds 'if (p7->d.data == NULL) { ERR_raise(...PKCS12_R_DECODE_ERROR); return NULL; }' and siblings. Recorded per instruction; not a spatial-safety bug and not an arena bug.

component: crypto/bn (GF(2^m) modular reduction) reached from crypto/ec low-level binary-curve APIs
affected_function: BN_GF2m_mod_arr (crypto/bn/bn_gf2m.c), fed by BN_GF2m_poly2arr; reached via EC_GROUP_new_curve_GF2m / EC_POINT_set_affine_coordinates and friends
trigger: An untrusted explicit GF(2^m) field polynomial with a zero constant term (an even BIGNUM), or with degree above OPENSSL_ECC_MAX_FIELD_BITS. BN_GF2m_poly2arr then produces an exponent array that never contains 0, so BN_GF2m_mod_arr's terminating loop condition 'p[k] != 0' never holds: it reads past the end of the exponent array and derives limb indices n from that garbage, then XORs into the result BIGNUM's limb array out of bounds.
poc: test/ec_internal_test.c - ec2m_field_sanity() added by the fix (rejects even pentanomial 0xf2, odd hexanomial 0xf3, and degree > OPENSSL_ECC_MAX_FIELD_BITS)
fixed_in: 3.3.3, 3.2.4, 3.1.8, 3.0.16 (1.1.1zb and 1.0.2zl for premium support customers only)
notes: Two distinct objects, both outside any arena. Primary (write): the result BIGNUM's limb array, crypto/bn/bn_gf2m.c:318 (openssl-3.0.15) 'z = r->d;' then the unbounded XOR stores at :338/:347 'z[j - n - 1] ^= (zz << d1);' and :375 'z[n + 1] ^= tmp_ulong;'. Allocation site: crypto/bn/bn_lib.c:281 'a = OPENSSL_zalloc(words * sizeof(*a));' in bn_expand_internal - one exact-sized malloc per BIGNUM (the sibling branch uses OPENSSL_secure_zalloc only under BN_FLG_SECURE, which public EC curve parameters do not set). Secondary (read): the exponent array itself, scanned past its end by :330/:366 'for (k = 1; p[k] != 0; k++)'; in BN_GF2m_mod that array is on the stack, crypto/bn/bn_gf2m.c:393 'int arr[6];', and in the EC path it is EC_GROUP::poly[6] embedded in the heap group object. Both the limb-array write and the stack-array read cross an object boundary a malloc/free-granularity or stack-canary checker sees. Branch cherry-picks: 3.0.16 72ae83ad214d2eef262461365a1975707f862712, 3.1.8 fdf6723362ca51bd883295efe206cb5b1cfa5154, 3.2.4 bc7e04d7c8d509fb78fc0e285aa948fb0da04700, 3.3.3 c0d3e4d32d2805f49bec30547f225bc4d092e1f4, 3.4.0 c47d9d7ec81bbab339d102bded809a558d0ebe6a.

trigger: AEAD-encrypted CMS whose ASN.1 IV OCTET STRING is longer than EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH: the first call returned the true length i, then the second get_octetstring_int(type,&tl,iv,i) wrote i (>16) bytes into the fixed stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH].
notes: Local 'unsigned char iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH];'. Fix passes EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH as the cap and adds 'if (i <= 0 || i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH) return -1;', removing the second unbounded fill. Overflow is of a stack array.

trigger: A BIO_f_linebuffer chained above a BIO that performs short writes: leftover input with no trailing newline was memcpy'd unconditionally into ctx->obuf past its size.
notes: ctx->obuf = OPENSSL_malloc(DEFAULT_LINEBUFFER_SIZE) (bf_lbuf.c:62, DEFAULT_LINEBUFFER_SIZE = 1024*10). Vulnerable code: 'memcpy(&(ctx->obuf[ctx->obuf_len]), in, inl); ctx->obuf_len += inl;' with no space check. Application-level buffering BIO, ordinary heap - not the record layer.

trigger: A TS/PKCS7 signed attribute whose SigningCertificate value is not an ASN.1 SEQUENCE: code read attr->value.sequence->data/length regardless of attr->type, treating the wrong union member as an ASN1_STRING.
notes: attr comes from PKCS7_get_signed_attribute() -> an ASN1_TYPE decoded onto the heap. Fix: 'if (attr == NULL || attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE) return NULL;' before 'p = attr->value.sequence->data;'. The confused object is a heap-allocated ASN1_TYPE union.

trigger: CMS PasswordRecipientInfo with a crafted encrypted key: the off-by-8 length check let tmp[0] exceed the decrypted buffer, so memcpy(out, tmp+4, tmp[0]) over-reads tmp by up to 8 bytes and over-writes out (key) by up to 4 bytes.
notes: tmp = OPENSSL_malloc(inlen) (cms_pwri.c ~205); out is key = OPENSSL_malloc(pwri->encryptedKey->length) in ossl_cms_RecipientInfo_pwri_crypt. Fix: 'if (inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0])' replaces 'if (inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4))'. Both buffers are ordinary OPENSSL_malloc heap.

trigger: A no_proxy/server string that is an escaped IPv6 literal '[...]' of length exactly NI_MAXHOST+1: strncpy(host, server+1, sl) fills the stack buffer with no room for a terminator, so the later strstr()/found[sl] scan reads past host.
notes: Local 'char host[NI_MAXHOST];'. Fix adds 'host[sl] = \'\0\';' after 'strncpy(host, server + 1, sl);'. Over-read is on a stack array, not any pool.

trigger: QUIC server: an Initial packet that validates via retry token but whose channel creation fails. port_bind_channel() transfers/releases the qrx, then port_default_packet_handler's 'undesirable:' path calls ossl_qrx_free(qrx) again.
notes: CHECKED PER INSTRUCTION: the double-freed object is the OSSL_QRX struct, allocated 'qrx = OPENSSL_zalloc(sizeof(OSSL_QRX))' (quic_record_rx.c:204), refcount-managed; fix adds ossl_qrx_newref/refcount. NOT URXE pool memory - the datagram element e is released exactly once via ossl_quic_demux_release_urxe(port->demux, e). So this is ordinary heap, not the quic-urxe-pool arena.

trigger: DANE client verification: with certain TLSA records the matched-cert slot was updated via 'OPENSSL_free(dane->mcert)' which raw-frees an X509 that is still reference-counted/referenced, leaving a dangling pointer -> use-after-free and/or double-free.
notes: dane->mcert holds an X509* (set via 'dane->mcert = cert; X509_up_ref(cert);'); X509 objects are OPENSSL_zalloc'd by X509_new. Fix: '-OPENSSL_free(dane->mcert); +X509_free(dane->mcert);' so the reference count is honoured. 3.6.2 CHANGES: 'Fixed potential use-after-free in DANE client code ... use-after-free and/or double-free on the client side' (CVE-2026-28387). Ordinary heap object; not an arena.

trigger: A very large buflen makes the length arithmetic (buflen*3, or 1+buflen*2) overflow size_t, so OPENSSL_malloc(tmp_n) under-allocates and the hex conversion writes past it.
notes: 'tmp_n = (sep != CH_ZERO) ? buflen * 3 : 1 + buflen * 2; tmp = OPENSSL_malloc(tmp_n)'. Fix adds SIZE_MAX/3 and (SIZE_MAX-1)/2 overflow guards. tmp is ordinary OPENSSL_malloc heap.

trigger: An ASN.1 primitive whose content length exceeds INT_MAX: the 'int len' parameter truncated the true 'long' length before it was handed to ASN1_STRING_set(stmp, cont, len), producing an ASN1_STRING whose recorded length disagrees with the buffer.
notes: Fix widens the signature to 'long len', computes 'int ilen = (int)len' and rejects 'len != (long)ilen' with ASN1_R_TOO_LONG before ASN1_STRING_set0/ASN1_STRING_set. The ASN1_STRING data buffer is OPENSSL_realloc heap (ASN1_STRING_set). Integer-truncation class; consequence is out-of-bounds access on that heap buffer.

trigger: TLS client with OCSP stapling enabled receiving a crafted stapled response whose OCSP_response_status != SUCCESSFUL: bs was OCSP_BASICRESP_free'd and then freed again at the shared 'end:' label.
notes: bs = OCSP_response_get1_basic(resp) (heap ASN1 object). On the non-successful path 'OCSP_BASICRESP_free(bs);' then falls to 'end:' which frees bs again; fix inserts 'bs = NULL;' after the first free. Double-free of ordinary heap object.

trigger: X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_email/add1_rfc822/smtputf8 with an email whose local part is longer than its domain: 'local_len = len - (at - name)' set local_len to the domain length, so dns_len = len - local_len - 1 = (local_len)-1 and validate_hostname_part(at+1, dns_len) scanned past the end of the name buffer.
notes: 'name' is the caller-supplied email buffer passed straight into validate_email_name (X509_VERIFY_PARAM_add1_rfc822: 'validate_email_name(email, len, 1)', not copied first). Fix: 'local_len = at - name;' and 'validate_local_part(name, local_len, ...)'. Over-read is on the application-provided string (ordinary heap/stack in the caller), not an OpenSSL arena.

trigger: PKCS7_verify() with caller-supplied indata: on the error/cleanup path 'if (indata != NULL) BIO_pop(p7bio); BIO_free_all(p7bio);' mishandled the internal BIO chain, freeing a BIO still referenced / freeing across the popped boundary.
notes: p7bio is the filter-BIO chain built by PKCS7_dataInit (each BIO_new -> OPENSSL_malloc). Fix replaces the pop+free_all with 'while (p7bio != NULL && p7bio != indata) { next = BIO_pop(p7bio); BIO_free(p7bio); p7bio = next; }'. Freed objects are ordinary heap BIOs.

trigger: CMS KeyAgreeRecipientInfo AES-WRAP-PAD key unwrap: on an integrity-failure path the AES unwrap primitive writes/cleanses up to inlen bytes, but the output buffer was sized to the (smaller) reported outlen, giving an 8-byte out-of-bounds write.
notes: 'out = OPENSSL_malloc(outlen)' undersized. Fix: 'outsize = (size_t)outlen < inlen ? inlen : (size_t)outlen; out = OPENSSL_malloc(outsize);'. out is ordinary OPENSSL_malloc heap (cms_kari.c, distinct from the cms_pwri.c bugs).

trigger: Direct caller of ASN1_mbstring_copy/ncopy with a huge BMPSTRING/UNIVERSALSTRING nchar: 'outlen = nchar << 1' / 'nchar << 2' overflows int (e.g. nchar==0x40000000 -> 0), OPENSSL_malloc(outlen+1) allocates 1 byte, then traverse_string writes 4*nchar bytes.
notes: 'outlen = nchar << 2;' then 'p = OPENSSL_malloc(outlen + 1); dest->data = p;' (a_mbstr.c:198,215,223). Fix rejects nchar > INT_MAX/2 (BMP) and INT_MAX/4 (UNIV), and guards the UTF-8 out_utf8 sum against INT_MAX overflow. Output ASN1_STRING data is ordinary heap.

trigger: CMS PWRI using a KEK cipher with block size < 4 (e.g. RC2/2-byte): the pre-decrypt sanity check only enforced inlen >= 2*blocklen, so the check-byte test read tmp[1]..tmp[6] beyond the inlen-sized tmp allocation.
notes: Distinct bug from CVE-2025-9230 in the same function. tmp = OPENSSL_malloc(inlen); read '((tmp[1]^tmp[4]) & (tmp[2]^tmp[5]) & (tmp[3]^tmp[6]))'. Fix changes 'if (blocklen <= 0)' to 'if (blocklen < 4)' guaranteeing inlen >= 7. Over-read on OPENSSL_malloc heap.
